title: Enterprise Financial Services AI Agent Implementation
description: A large financial services company is interested in implementing Glean AI Agents to streamline their customer onboarding process. They have complex compliance requirements and need to integrate with multiple existing systems. The customer is technically sophisticated but concerned about data security and governance.
learningObjectives: Demonstrate understanding of Glean AI Agent architecture
Explain how agent governance works in regulated industries
Configure agents to integrate with existing enterprise systems
Present business value of agent implementation

stages.title: Discovery Call
stages.description: Initial discovery call with the customer's IT and business stakeholders to understand their needs
stages.challenge: The CIO asks: 'We've tried other AI solutions before, but they couldn't handle our complex compliance requirements. How does Glean's AI Agent approach differ, especially regarding data security and governance?'
expectedElements: Acknowledge previous AI challenges in financial services
Explain Glean's security and governance architecture
Describe how agent permissions work
Ask follow-up questions about specific compliance concerns
technicalPoints: Glean's active data and AI governance with continuous scanning
commonMistakes: Focusing only on features without addressing compliance
Not asking about their specific regulatory requirements
Overcommitting on compliance capabilities
Being too vague about security measures

stages.title: Technical Solution Demonstration
stages.description: Follow-up meeting to demonstrate how Glean AI Agents would work in their environment
stages.challenge: The Enterprise Architect asks: 'Can you show us specifically how we would configure an agent to handle our customer onboarding process? It needs to verify customer identity, check against our compliance database, and create accounts in three different systems.'
expectedElements: Demonstrate the agent builder interface
Show how to configure multi-step workflows
Explain how agents connect to multiple systems
Discuss how to test and validate agent configurations
technicalPoints: Agentic reasoning engine for multi-step workflows
commonMistakes: Not showing a concrete example
Glossing over technical integration details
Failing to address how errors are handled
Not explaining the testing process

stages.title: Security Objection Handling
stages.description: Meeting with the CISO who has concerns about data access
stages.challenge: The CISO interrupts: 'I'm concerned about giving AI agents broad access to our systems. What happens if someone configures an agent incorrectly and it accesses or shares sensitive customer financial data?'
expectedElements: Acknowledge the valid concern
Explain the defense-in-depth approach
Detail the specific preventive controls
Describe monitoring and remediation capabilities
technicalPoints: Role-based access controls for agent creators
Active governance with sensitive data scanning
commonMistakes: Dismissing the concern as unlikely
Providing only general assurances
Not addressing the specific scenario mentioned
Failing to explain monitoring capabilities

stages.title: Implementation Planning Session
stages.description: Working session to create an implementation roadmap
stages.challenge: The project manager asks: 'What would a realistic implementation timeline look like? We need to prioritize customer onboarding first, then expand to other use cases. How should we phase this approach?'
expectedElements: Outline a phased implementation approach
Recommend starting with a limited pilot
Detail key milestones and dependencies
Discuss resource requirements and training
commonMistakes: Proposing an unrealistic timeline
Not accounting for testing and validation
Overlooking change management needs
Failing to identify dependencies on other systems

stages.title: Executive Value Presentation
stages.description: Presentation to executive stakeholders on expected ROI and business impact
stages.challenge: The CFO asks: 'What specific metrics should we track to measure the success of this implementation, and what ROI can we expect in the first year?'
expectedElements: Present relevant case studies from financial services
Recommend specific KPIs to track
Provide a framework for calculating ROI
Set realistic expectations for first-year returns
commonMistakes: Using generic ROI statistics not specific to their use case
Overpromising on financial returns
Not tying metrics to their specific business goals
Failing to address implementation and maintenance costs
